label: early copy steps (outputs 2-3) when "i" is the current or next output
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, never on original-phase or <DEL> steps, and almost entirely on the 2nd and 3rd copy outputs (recall_idx 1-2 hold about 89% of mass; recall_idx 3 adds about 9%). Within that window it strongly prefers steps where the token being output or the next one to output is "i" (out_tok=i lift 19x, next_out=i lift 17x). The strongest activations are on sequences like "y g i i i ..." and "i i i i", where orig(2) is i and i repeats, and they peak on the step right before the i run gets output. It also fires only when the input token has already appeared (in_first=0, which is always true in the copy phase). Its weaker preferences are for inputs j/u/i/a/g and outputs j/g/2/r/p, which gives a broad low-magnitude tail. The "i" clause by itself gets only about 47% recall and 36% precision, and many early copy steps with i upcoming stay silent, so this is an incomplete, partly distributed description.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: orig4=i (+3.32), orig3=i (+3.31), orig0=i (+3.18), prev3_tok=<DEL> (+2.85), orig1=i (+2.72), phase=2 & out_tok=j (+2.65). Lower it: prev_tok=i (-4.41), in_first=1 (-4.00), phase=0 (-3.46), orig3=e (-3.21).
